title: Lesson 7 - Sensitive Data: Identify/Classify PCI, PII, HIPAA; Shield Platform Encryption; Field History; Data Protection
description: Given a scenario, determine the appropriate access controls to protect sensitive data (PCI, PII, HIPAA) and understand Shield Platform Encryption.

questions.question: A customer stores credit-card numbers and wants to minimize exposure if a backup or export leaks. Which control specifically protects data at rest?
options: Shield Platform Encryption on the card field
Remove the field from page layouts
questions.explanation: Shield Platform Encryption encrypts the field at rest so leaked/exported data is unusable. FLS, OWD, and layouts restrict which users can see it but do not protect the underlying stored data.

questions.question: Which combination best protects a PII field end to end?
options: Classify it, hide via FLS, encrypt with Shield, and audit changes with field history
Only set the org-wide default to Private
questions.explanation: Layered protection - classify, restrict (FLS), encrypt at rest (Shield), and audit (field history) - is the model for sensitive data. Any single declarative change leaves a gap.

questions.question: Why does enabling Shield Platform Encryption alone NOT stop an internal user from seeing a sensitive field?
options: Encryption protects data at rest but does not restrict which authorized users can read the field
Shield only works on standard fields
questions.explanation: Encryption is about protecting stored data from exposure/breach; user visibility is governed by FLS and sharing, which must be configured separately.
